Yes. Set it up as a local secret—do not paste the key into chat or commit it.

From the project root, install fal’s JavaScript client:

```bash
cd frontend
npm install @fal-ai/client
```

Store the key only in your terminal session:

```bash
read -s FAL_KEY
export FAL_KEY
```

Or persist it locally in a gitignored `.env.local` file:

```env
FAL_KEY=your_fal_key_here
```

Important: don’t use `VITE_FAL_KEY`; Vite would expose it to every browser visitor. Image generation should run through a server-side script or backend endpoint that reads `FAL_KEY`.

fal’s client is `@fal-ai/client`, and it uses `fal.subscribe()` to submit generation prompts. [fal’s official JavaScript setup](https://docs.fal.ai/documentation/development/getting-started/deploy-your-first-image-generator)

Yes. The right setup is:

1. You give me only names.
